title: Functions on Graphs Core Test
description: Interpret representations, explain misconceptions, and transfer reasoning to unfamiliar cases.

questions.questionText: A plotted point on a function is (2, 6). What output belongs to this input?
questions.explanation: The horizontal coordinate 2 is the input. The vertical coordinate 6 is the output.

questions.questionText: A graph consists only of the points (0, 2), (1, 2), (2, 2). Is y a function of x?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; each x has exactly one y.
questions.explanation: A horizontal set of points may share a height. No input has conflicting outputs.
options: No; repeated heights are forbidden.
Yes; each x has exactly one y.
No; functions must slope upward.
Yes; all point collections are functions.

questions.questionText: Two plotted points are (2, 1) and (2, 4). Why can no function of x contain both?
questions.correctAnswer: The vertical line x = 2 meets two different points.
questions.explanation: Different y-values only cause a conflict when their x-values agree. A vertical line holds the input fixed.
options: The points have different y-values.
The graph must contain the origin.
A function can have only one point.
The vertical line x = 2 meets two different points.

questions.questionText: The entire graph is the horizontal line y = 2. Does it pass the vertical-line test?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; every vertical line meets it once.
questions.explanation: Use vertical, not horizontal, test lines. Each x gives the single output shown by the horizontal line.
options: Yes; every vertical line meets it once.
No; a horizontal line meets it infinitely often.
No; its slope is zero.
Yes; it has no output.

questions.questionText: The entire graph is the vertical line x = 2. Is it a function of x?
questions.correctAnswer: No; one x has many y-values.
questions.explanation: All points on a vertical line share one input while their outputs vary. Straightness alone does not establish a function.
options: Yes; it is a straight line.
Yes; x stays constant.
No; one x has many y-values.
No; every straight line fails.

questions.questionText: A function graph is a straight line through (0, 2) and (2, 8). What is its output at x = 1?
questions.explanation: Halfway between x = 0 and x = 2, the height is halfway between 2 and 8: 5. The stated straight line justifies interpolation.

questions.questionText: A graph has only the three solid points (1, 2), (3, 3), (5, 4). Are inputs between these points included?
questions.correctAnswer: No; only inputs 1, 3, and 5 are shown as part of this graph.
questions.explanation: A discrete graph contains only its plotted points unless connecting segments or a larger rule are specified.
options: Yes; automatically join every point.
Yes; all real inputs belong to every function.
No; isolated points cannot define a function.
No; only inputs 1, 3, and 5 are shown as part of this graph.

questions.questionText: At x = 2, a graph has an open circle at y = 2 and a solid point at y = 5. Every other allowed x has one solid graph point. Does this graph define y as a function of x?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; the open circle is excluded, leaving one output at that input.
questions.explanation: An open circle marks an excluded endpoint. Only the solid point supplies an output at this input.
options: No; open circles count as outputs.
Yes; the open circle is excluded, leaving one output at that input.
No; one missing point invalidates every function.
Yes; two included outputs would also be allowed.

questions.correctAnswer: Yes; the vertical-line test passes.
questions.explanation: A curve can assign one y per x. Horizontal repeats indicate shared outputs, which are allowed.
options: Yes; the vertical-line test passes.
No; any horizontal repeat breaks a function.
No; only straight graphs are functions.
Yes; every curve is a function.

options: Yes; every reflection preserves the function property.

questions.questionText: A graph includes y = x for x < 2 and y = x + 2 for x >= 2. What happens at the join?
questions.correctAnswer: Only output 4 is included at x = 2, so there is no conflict.
questions.explanation: The first condition excludes the boundary input; the second includes it. A jump does not prevent a graph from defining a function.
options: Both 2 and 4 are included, so it fails.
Only output 4 is included at x = 2, so there is no conflict.
Only output 2 is included.
No output is included at x = 2.

questions.questionText: A circle centered at (0, 0) has radius 2. A student tests only the vertical line x = 2, which touches once, and declares it a function. What disproves the claim?

questions.explanation: Every vertical line must meet at most once. A single counterexample is enough to reject a graph, while one passing line is not enough to accept it.
options: One successful test line proves the claim.
The circle has no points at x = 0.
At x = 0, the circle has outputs 2 and -2.
Only horizontal lines may be used.

options: Their outputs at the shared input must be equal.
The two segments must have equal slopes.

The shared input must be deleted.
